standard_prerequisites.name: Soberness of schemes and finiteness of the fibres of the projections
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: Schemes, the lemma that schemes are sober; Same chapter, the lemma that the fibres of the projections of the presentation are finite

core_obligations: Reduce to a single quasi-compact etale chart (proof lines 2086-2092): by the local nature of soberness and the characterization of Zariski local quasi-separatedness, one may assume there is an affine scheme U with a surjective quasi-compact etale morphism to X; setting R equal to U x_X U with its two projections, the fibres of the projections are finite by the presentation lemma, so the Kolmogorov criterion for finite fibre quotients applies and the quotient space is Kolmogorov.

Find a generic point for an irreducible closed subset (proof lines 2094-2110): let T be an irreducible closed subset; by the reduced closed subspace lemma there is a closed subspace Z with underlying set T, and the base change of the chart to Z is again a quasi-compact surjective etale morphism from an affine scheme, so Z is Zariski locally quasi-separated; the open dense subscheme proposition then provides an open dense subspace Z' of Z which is a scheme.

Conclude (proof lines 2110-2116): the underlying set of Z' is open dense in T and irreducible because T is, so Z' is an irreducible scheme, hence its underlying space is the closure of a single point by soberness of schemes, and that point is a generic point of T, so the space is sober.
proof_roadmap: Reduce to a single affine etale chart and conclude that the space is Kolmogorov from the finite fibre criterion.
For an irreducible closed subset, realize it by a closed subspace and find an open dense subscheme of that subspace.
Use soberness of schemes on that subscheme to produce a generic point of the original closed subset.
difficulty_reason: The lemma proves that the underlying topological space of a Zariski locally quasi-separated algebraic space is sober (statement lines 2079-2084). The proof (proof lines 2086-2125) reduces to a single affine etale chart and applies the finite fibre Kolmogorov criterion, then for an irreducible closed subset produces a closed subspace with an open dense subscheme and uses soberness of schemes to obtain a generic point. H3: a two-stage reduction with a genuine use of the scheme case on a dense subscheme, written out in full.
